items.t: A navbar on every page, a map with pictures, and one window for every way in

The what's-new count is now bright and hard to miss, and reading mode gained text sizes and shorter lines.

items.t: Faster home page images
items.s: The home tiles load much faster: they're now 800px WebP images, and files that never change are cached for a year.
items.x: Notable TL;DR: The home tiles load much faster: they're now 800px WebP images, and files that never change are cached for a year. Read the full story Renan converted the landing tiles from full size originals to WebP at 800px on the longest side. According to the notes kept with the original artwork, that took the eight tiles from about 14.4 MB to about 350 KB. Fingerprinted assets (files whose names change whenever their content does) are now cached by browsers for a year.

items.t: How this AstroLog works
items.s: Where the changelog's source lives, how it reaches this public page, and how to add an entry.
items.x: TL;DR: Entries are Markdown files in a private repository. On every change, a workflow builds the site and publishes only the finished pages to a public repository, which GitHub Pages serves. Read the full write up Two repositories changelog astro (private) holds the Markdown entries, the library, and the site's source. changelog astro public (public) holds only the built pages and the README. A workflow in the private repository runs on every push. It builds the site with Astro, removes every source folder from the history, adds back only the built pages, and pushes the result to the public repository. items.t: The perforated sheet
items.s: How orgspirituality.org draws its home page as one perforated blotter sheet, and why the perforations are masks rather than borders.
items.x: TL;DR: The nine home tiles touch edge to edge, and the perforations are drawn as overlay layers on top of the whole grid, cut into dashes with CSS masks. That keeps every dash the same size on any screen. Read the full write up Where it started The home page has always been a grid of nine sections with ORG at the center. In June 2026 Tripp made the tiles touch, with no gaps, so the grid reads as a single sheet instead of nine cards. The perforation stopped being a border around each tile and became one drawing across the whole grid. How it is drawn today The code lives in BlotterPerforations.tsx in org frontend.
